novel.justification: This note maintains a single curvature floor over the compact preference path, which is stronger than FangRidderXie2026's pointwise Hessian condition at one fixed penalty. Bounded features and outcomes, benchmark weights bounded away from zero, and the three-derivative condition make \(c\mapsto H_c\) continuous along a continuous optimizer path; positive definiteness at every \(c\in\mathcal C\) then yields \(h>0\) by compactness. A concrete benchmark-near sufficient design has a uniform positive eigenvalue floor for the centered-feature covariance on the optimizer neighborhood, a neighborhood small enough to control the third-cumulant term in the KL Hessian, and a welfare-Hessian upper bound strictly smaller than \(c_{\min}\) times the resulting KL-curvature floor.
